ShortDescription.Value: Fix Not Enough Customers icons by balancing commercial shop production and shopping demand.

Publish.LongDescription:
# 🛒
## "Not Enough Customers" everywhere?
Adding more citizens doesn't always help!
### Why?
* Facts: NEC icons appear when a commercial shop is over **90%+ unused Service** (different from total stock). * Commercial shop workers get paid to produce Service. Service is different from goods (e.g., food, paper...) you see delivered. * Problem 1: Vanilla puts **50%–100% full shops in the same bucket**. A shop at critical 91% full doesn't really get prioritized over a shop at lower 52% full which is safe from triggering any floating icon. * So citizens can keep going to healthier shops while desperate shops are still ignored that are 90% + full. The system is unaware of the NEC icon trigger point for citizen shop selection. * Problem 2: vanilla does slow worker production a little starting at 80% full Service to help out. But by 90% critical threshold, it's still producing too much. * Vanilla doesn't clamp production to 0% until the shop hits full 100%, way too late to prevent NEC icons. * In real life, commercial work rate is reduced at times when high Service rates are not needed because no shoppers. * Problem 3: cims at work/school can not shop, so we get peak periods with a lot less eligible shoppers. Only elderly or adults not in school/work are available during that time.
**Shops workers end up making excess Service product faster than current available shoppers can use it.** Adding more citizens didn't fix this for many players when the 90%+ shops aren't also getting prioritized for visits.
### Some mod test results (aka stop pulling your hair out)
* **130k city:** 165 NEC -> only 4 after ~30 minutes. * **90k city:** 335 NEC -> only 30 after 10 min., 9 after 20 min.
### What to expect
* Just install the mod and play! No Options menu or settings to configure. * Give cities 15–30 minutes. Many changes happen within 5 minutes. * After 30+ minutes, if you have a few 10-20 left over, now is time to prune a few shops. Don't need to prune the exact left over shops. * It won't fix every case of legit excess commercial zoning or poor access to shops. * Safe to remove, Vanilla takes over again. No Harmony patch means more compatible with other mods and the game. * Companion [mod City Watchdog](https://mods.paradoxplaza.com/mods/144908/Windows) recommended to easily see totals go up/down like shown in the screenshot. Make sure to put a "blue star" next to Not Enough Customers. * This mod is a temp fix until IFS is able to fix/balance/prioritize commercial businesses exploding in Not Enough Customers Icons.
### Support and Feedback
* Best way to support is click the **LIKE 👍** button (top right)! No donations, just a free like for the many days of work. * Feedback is welcome on [Discord](https://discord.gg/gwXgvtyhjc) or GitHub where the source code is (see icon links on the right). GPL3 License.
### How does the mod work?
* **Starts helping when shop hits ~82% full Service**, before the critical 90% threshold causes an alert icon. I tested many rates to optimize for realistic rate buckets and 82%+ worked well to slow production until shoppers naturally reduce service levels. * Once healthy again (below 82%), it goes back to vanilla to handle normally. * Just like real life, shops reduce worker production at times of day when there are not enough shoppers to reduce service levels. No fake shoppers are made; balancing your existing cims is often enough to fix it. * **Leisure** businesses are also helped (Meals, Entertainment, Recreation). * Hotels: best-effort balancing using existing tourists. Hotel NEC icons depends on both excess unused Service and too many empty rooms. NEC-Fix helps struggling hotels hit safer occupancy levels without creating fake tourists.
#### Notes * Problem 4: full commercial demand bar doesn't mean your citizens can support more. It means companies are looking for spaces. You don't need to build more just because you see a full bar. * **Adaptive pricing:** yes, vanilla makes struggling shops slightly more attractive through lower prices. A shop with 91% unused Service gets a price multiplier of 0.754×, compared with 0.988× at 52%. But despite vanilla's price weights, test cities still had hundreds of NEC warnings so slightly lower pricing is not influencing citizens effectively. More important, a separate **shopping-selection score Stops Adjusting beyond 50% unused Service**. That's what I mean by shops 50% - 100% levels being in the same bucket so our 91% shop doesn't get the real **direct** priority it needs.
